key_insight: A physics-informed neural network can learn depth-averaged avalanche dynamics from the Savage-Hutter model, matching 1D analytical benchmarks and extending to realistic 2D granular-collapse experiments.
engineering_relevance: This provides a compact surrogate for avalanche prediction that can support hazard assessment by estimating flow depth, velocity, and runout patterns with limited data.
method: Verified the PINN on three 1D problems: prescribed-velocity height prediction, prescribed-height velocity prediction, and fully coupled conservative-form learning.
Extended the framework to 2D and used a hybrid physics + sparse-data loss, since pure physics training collapsed to the trivial zero solution.
Compared predictions against laboratory experiments and TITAN2D using RMSE, peak fields, and wetted-area IoU.
evidence_signal: In 2D validation, global height RMSE was 2.7–6.7 mm across four cases and mean wetted-area IoU reached 69–81%, while the coupled 1D PINN achieved height and velocity RMSEs of 0.043 and 0.079 in non-dimensional units.
watch_item: Pure physics-only training failed in 2D, so the approach depends on a small amount of sparse observational data and careful loss balancing to avoid trivial solutions.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Depth-Averaged Avalanche Dynamics
